slot_note: re-root after portal round 1 on architecture 2 (2026-10-26, both responses on the v2 golden) and nine candidates set aside on Opus call-only probes; wave 7 slot numbered from seed FC37, whose world is not kept: the new draw is a construction project-management software company's 2027 new paying customers by sales region, drawn without a seed under the author's ruling of 2026-10-26 (no retiring and no pausing; new worlds and new stump strategies allowed)
niche: a construction project-management SaaS placing its 2027 onboarding pod with the regional sales team expected to add the most new paying customers in calendar 2027, when about two in five new customers are founded by people who left a paying customer for a contractor not yet on the software
answer: Place the 2027 onboarding pod with the Southwest team: it is expected to add about 600 new paying customers in calendar 2027 (to the nearest 200), the most of the six regions, and Texas & Gulf comes second.
analyst_test: With both billing systems stitched, divisions, reactivations and voided first invoices removed and the March 2024 territory map applied, the easy route fits each region's monthly new paying customers on its own trend, season and marketing spend, picks the form by back-test, finds the customer-referral lead source small and flat, and names Texas & Gulf at about 500 with the Southwest second; it never links a new workspace's first user to the people who left paying customers, so the Southwest's April to September 2026 surge of departing project staff, who found new customers through 2027, never enters it.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is each region's 2027 new paying customers, which product-adoption analysis forecasts as organic acquisition plus the adoption users carry to a new organisation when they change jobs, measured by linking each new workspace's founding admin to departures from paying workspaces and projected as a lagged yield on departures; with a hospital's or a utility's nouns there is no workspace founded by a former user and no adoption carried by a job move, so the task stops making sense.

driver: Next period's new members include organisations founded by people who left an existing member for one not yet served, at a yield and a lag that linking the records shows; a forecast from each group's own arrival history, trend, season and spend misses a recent surge of departures from one group's members, which arrives as new members through the following year.
driver_concrete: About two in five of Plinthwise's new paying customers are founded by someone who left a paying customer for a contractor not yet on the software, a median of 11 months later and close to nine times in ten in the same region; between April and September 2026 the Southwest's customers removed about four times their usual number of users, so the Southwest adds about 600 new paying customers in 2027 (to the nearest 200) against about 480 for Texas & Gulf, which leads every forecast on the regions' own history.
stump: The default path stitches the two billing systems, counts new paying customers by the memo's rules on the 2024 map, fits each region's own trend, season and marketing spend by back-test, finds the referral lead source small and flat, and names Texas & Gulf at about 500 with the Southwest second; the step that lands it there is forecasting the Southwest from its own arrivals, when about two in five new customers are founded by people who left paying customers a median of 11 months earlier, and the Southwest's customers removed about four times their usual number of users between April and September 2026, who found new customers through 2027 and put the Southwest first at about 600.

differentiation.task306: task306 forecasts failures in an asset base still taking in old units its roll does not yet hold; here no unit is missing from a roll: next year's new members are organisations founded by people who left existing members, at a yield and a lag the linked record shows, so a surge of departures, not an arriving cohort's age, carries the forward count
differentiation.task468: task468's earlier architectures cost the units active today by how long their spell has run; here nothing is costed per active unit: next year's new members are forecast from the people leaving existing members, each founder linked to the departure that seeded it, a lagged yield no tenure curve carries
differentiation.task98: task98 v6 counts units under a score threshold after a classifier change; here no threshold or classifier moves: the forward count adds the new members founded by existing members' leavers, a lagged yield on departures recovered by linking records across organisations

lineage.fate: spent: portal round 1 (2026-10-25) landed by both responses, each designating fixed-rate commercial real estate at the golden $150 million; conditioning each balloon's extension on refinance cover at the planning rate is a reflex for the portal's models, so the slot re-roots
lineage.driver: Two parts of a stock answer the same forward terms in opposite directions: one, whose units hold rates the terms now beat, leaves faster than its own past, while the other, whose units fall due inside the window, keeps every due unit whose own earnings no longer cover the terms it would have to roll onto, at a share read from past due dates by that cover; the part with the most exposure over the window is found only when both answers are projected, because the schedule, a recent share or a price gap leaves the second part running off and names a third part that is neither.
lineage.driver_concrete: Carrick Valley's fixed-rate CRE pool holds about $2.6 billion of balloons falling due from December 2026 through 2027, nearly all written in the push of December 2021 to April 2022 at the credit box's full proceeds on pro forma rents, half of them interest only; over nine-tenths of that principal is expected to take the bank's one extension (36 months, a tenth paid down, the rest at the posted rate on 25-year amortization) because those properties' latest reviewed income no longer covers a new 25-year loan of the balloon at the planning cycle's 6.95 per cent, the cover below which (about 1.09) the bank's record of maturities since 2015 shows loans extending; the CRE pool's +200 bp loss averaged over the swap's first year is then $150 million, the largest of the five, while every route that repays the balloons when due, at the recent extension share, by rate gap, by property type, by the note-rate DSCR, by in-place cover or by the watch list designates the agency MBS.
lineage.stump: A strong solver prepays the 2023-24 mortgages on an incentive curve fitted to the bank's own loan history at the planning rate, runs the CRE loans to their contractual maturities and designates the agency MBS; the step that lands it there is paying the 2027 CRE balloons off on schedule (or at the recent extension share, or by rate gap), when the bank's maturity record shows that loans whose property income no longer covers a new loan at the prevailing CRE rate take the bank's one 36-month extension, and over nine-tenths of the 2027 wall's principal is such loans.

lineage.fate: spent: portal round 1 on architecture 2 (2026-10-26) landed by both responses, each opening the pilot in Muskegon and the North at about $40 million with the Lakeshore second; the whole-stack refinance incentive chosen over the own-rate and first-only curves on fit and back-test is a reflex for the portal's models, so the slot re-roots
lineage.driver: A junior unit leaves when the whole stack it belongs to is replaced or sold, and the holder replaces the stack when its blended price, each layer weighted by its size, rises above the price of one new senior unit; read off the junior's own price, or off the senior's alone, the exits validate on a record where a stack with a high-priced layer was high-priced throughout, and they miss a forward book whose largest juniors sit on small, cheap seniors, which lock nothing because they are small.
lineage.driver_concrete: Muskegon and the north's 1,460 equity taps of 2023 to 2026 ($70,000 to $112,000 at 8.1 to 9.4 per cent) sit behind first mortgages opened from 2010 to 2015 at 3.5 to 4.75 per cent with $65,000 to $125,000 left, so the debt on each house carries a blended rate of about 6.3 to 6.6 per cent: quiet while the posted 30-year rate held at 6.6 to 7.3 per cent through 2024 to 2026, and in the money from February 2027 as the planning cycle's base case takes it from 6.45 to 5.20 per cent; the region's members then pay off about $40 million of fixed-rate home equity principal in 2027, where the own-rate S-curve names Grand Rapids (about $60 million), the first mortgage's own incentive names the Lakeshore and the trailing payoffs name Kalamazoo and Battle Creek.
lineage.stump: A strong solver fits the home equity payoffs on each loan's own note rate against the posted home equity rate, a curve the 2019 to 2026 payoffs support, and names Grand Rapids at about $60 million, or reads the lock-in off each first mortgage's own rate and names the Lakeshore; the step that lands it there is reading a second lien's payoff off one of the two loans, when a member pays the second off by refinancing the whole debt on the house, which the stack's blended rate at the two balances against the posted 30-year rate decides: Muskegon and the north's large 2024 to 2026 taps sit behind small seasoned firsts at 3.5 to 4.75 per cent, so its stacks blend near 6.5 per cent and come into the money as the planning path falls, and it pays off about $40 million.
